pr.title: Edit translations in the selected board and card language
pr.body:
## Summary

Parents selecting Russian for a board could hear Russian while its editor preview and primary card fields still showed English. Translation fields existed farther down the card dialog, making corrections difficult to follow.

The board and card editors now show the selected language in their main controls. Corrections survive switching, saving and reloading while preserving source words, other languages and fixed cards. Saved corrections require an explicit AI replacement decision; audio follows the exact selected words and language.

Closes #32. Targets current **master**; no unmerged prerequisite.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed on the current build | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select Russian, correct a card, switch languages, save and reload; enter directly from Play. | Main controls show Russian and retain corrections. Source English, Spanish, fixed cards and media remain intact. Cancel discards drafts. | Matched pairs below and [browser checks](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/records/qa-r1-review-browser.log). |
| Clear both Russian fields, switch Spanish, and try Save/Duplicate; then cancel or complete the draft and reload. | Save refuses incomplete fields and Duplicate is disabled. Manual and legacy saved words remain intact; completed corrections persist with source/Spanish/media unchanged. | [17 focused browser scenarios](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/records/qa-r1-review-browser.log) and [refusal capture](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/after-empty-correction-refused.png). |
| Delay audio, change words/language, then fail and retry; fail a local save. | Old audio never appears ready for new input. Retry uses corrected Russian; label-only changes reuse speech. Failed writes stay visibly unsaved and retry persists them. | [Failure capture](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/after-corrected-audio-failure.png) and controlled-response browser checks. |
| Change source words, cancel/retry translation preparation, and review AI wording. | Saved corrections remain for review. AI replacement requires a separate draft-bound choice; manual and AI source-language collisions are refused, including corrections made in the same unsaved draft. | [Replacement review](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/after-ai-replacement-review.png), [AI refusal](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/after-ai-source-collision.png), [manual refusal](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/after-manual-source-collision.png), and passing merge/browser regressions. |
| Visit and cancel account login after a correction; round-trip an account snapshot and sync conflict. | Guest edits survive navigation/reload; snapshot and conflict copies preserve correction provenance and exact audio keys. | Focused browser/unit checks; current CI also exercises account backup/restore. |

### Before / After

Actual master `fabb925cf5ee11171d5668af7c2bab44ec9fc613` to captured runtime `b064097ac6a02717adfd7507d8d4cd741353069c`. Current head `6990cbbbeeb70c0c77d50b9c5e15a1fb835c183f` adds four JSDoc lines only; the tested behavior and captures remain applicable. Fresh isolated builds in Edge 154 on Windows use the same synthetic English/Russian/Spanish library, account-entry setup, 1180×1000 viewport, scale 1, light theme and controlled starting clock. Play labels intentionally remain English; fixed Sheep stays English.

| Before: actual master | After: proposed change |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: source labels in board editor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/before-board.png?raw=true) | ![After: selected Russian label with fixed Sheep preserved](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/after-board.png?raw=true) |
| ![Before: English primary card fields](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/before-card.png?raw=true) | ![After: Russian primary card fields](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/after-card.png?raw=true) |

The pairs show the selected language becoming visible in the main workflow. The baseline already had [lower translation controls](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/captures/before-existing-translation-controls.png). Both card captures start at the Position row. [Bound provenance](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/README.md) identifies source, served bundles, fixture, harness and image hashes. Providers/voices are controlled, fullscreen neutralized, and service workers blocked equally to exclude stale bundles/PWA notices; no compared UI or image pixels were edited.

## Supporting checks and limitations

Passed: 299 unit tests, TypeScript, release-contract checks, server/web builds and final Android export. All 17 affected translation browser scenarios passed, including manual/legacy empty-draft validation. Another 105 previously passing browser scenarios remain applicable under the [impact assessment](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/README.md). [Final-head CI](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37831814422) passed, including service/account integration and account browser checks. [Engineering review](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/38#issuecomment-6067487045) completed with no major issues on this exact head; prior findings remain fixed.

iOS bundle export failed on actual master and the integrated build because the unchanged Apple authentication dependency cannot resolve `prop-types`; [matched failure logs](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/c2331b99cc3bc6a71b84ac79442beb8fc45e6222/refresh/README.md) preserve the existing baseline problem for separate coordination. Native-device/emulator and live-provider execution remain unrun; [native checks are deferred](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/405#issuecomment-6041659686). GitHub rendered-page inspection is [waived](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/405#issuecomment-6022754087); genuine captures were inspected. [Independent QA](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/38#issuecomment-6066929182) assessed the previous head and found the empty-draft deletion (R1) and iOS export gap (E1). R1 is corrected and tested here; the same QA owner must reassess the final source, body and evidence. E1 remains open and unwaived under separate issue43/PR44.

[Complete twelve-commit/15-file scope and retained original descriptions](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/6aa90658b6de8a015f955f386bafce365d996c83/qa-r1-final/README.md). Historical stack and capture records remain preserved separately.

dependency44.title: Restore iOS export with the missing Apple authentication runtime dependency
dependency44.body:
## Summary

Little Say's iOS JavaScript export fails because Apple authentication imports `prop-types`, but the installed dependency graph does not provide it. Declare it as a mobile production dependency so clean locked installations can bundle the existing Apple authentication code.

The lockfile adds only `prop-types` 15.8.1 and its required nested `react-is` 16.13.1. Existing package versions, integrity hashes and classifications are unchanged; no provider code changes are needed.

Closes #43.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install baseline and final source independently with `npm ci`, then resolve the import from AppleButton and export iOS. | Baseline fails with missing `prop-types`. Final resolves version 15.8.1 and its required APIs, then completes the full iOS JavaScript export. Neither installation uses copied or junctioned dependencies. | [Before/After output and reproduction](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/README.md#before-and-after-observable-contract) |
| Export Android/web and run repository checks from the fresh final installation. | Both exports pass, along with 288 tests, type checks, server build and release metadata validation. | [Native exports](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/issue43-native-exports.log) · [Repository checks](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/issue43-check.log) |

This is non-UI dependency resolution; real CLI output is the observable Before/After contract. [Provenance](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/59a85fcf200da63e3a470c8e7847bab347a67161/provenance.json) binds actual master `fabb925c`, final source `a570b52c`, independent installations, commands and bundle hashes.

## Limitations

JavaScript export success does not establish a signed iOS build, TestFlight readiness, device behavior or real Apple sign-in. Those checks were not performed. No credentials, provider setup, cloud build, release or deployment is included.

Implementing task: `01a11ca6-7faa-7628-8031-ac89bc018019`. Independent review and CI results are recorded in the PR discussion.

issue.title: Show editable translations for the selected board and card language
issue.body:
## Problem

Parents can select Russian for speech while the board preview and primary card fields still show English. Translation fields exist farther down the card editor, making it difficult to see and correct the selected language consistently.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Show the selected editing language's labels and spoken words in both editors, including direct entry from Play. Keep original-language metadata and play-label preferences separate.
- Preserve corrections through language switches, save/reopen/reload and account context changes. Keep original words, other languages, IDs/order, media and fixed-language cards intact. Cancel must discard unsaved changes.
- Identify missing/stale translations honestly. Retain saved corrections for review after source edits; never pass source English off as a translation or silently delete variants.
- Protect manual and legacy translations during preparation and AI merges. Replacement needs an explicit reviewed decision. Manual or AI source-language changes must not hide a protected translation.
- Bind generated/preview audio and asynchronous results to exact spoken text, language, card and revision. Label-only edits may reuse matching audio; delayed or cancelled work must not affect another variant.
- Failed saves and translation/audio requests must retain corrections and support retry. Preserve consent, automatic-audio preferences and existing account backup/restore behavior.

## Implementation plan

1. Reuse the existing board/card editors and per-language storage with one explicit editing-language context and guarded variant updates.
2. Preserve manual corrections in translation/proposal merges and share source-language collision validation across manual and AI paths.
3. Validate editor entry, correction persistence, cancellation/retry, exact audio identity and account integration. Compare genuine current-master and proposed UI builds; native-device execution remains deferred.

Original requirements, detailed plan and superseded stack context are preserved in the [original issue record](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/c2331b99cc3bc6a71b84ac79442beb8fc45e6222/refresh/records/issue-body-before-refresh.md) and [source analysis](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/issues/32#issuecomment-6029282445). Prompt extraction, release retirement and unrelated playback work remain separate.

## Implementing Codex task

Current replacement implementation owner: verified task `01a11cbb-ec94-715f-a3e4-7aa82a416016`. The original owner's task and checkpoint are preserved in the linked historical record.

## Implementing PR

[PR #38 — Edit translations in the selected board and card language](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/38) (draft), targeting current master. PR34 and PR36 are merged; there is no unmerged prerequisite. Independent QA and review readiness remain coordinator-owned.

issueComments.body:
Source analysis and implementation design (planning only)

**Authority and evidence boundary.** The direct human request delegated through coordinator task `01a0f838-69d6-75b3-8cc0-f768175aa03e` is: "board and individual-card editor language selection changes speech generation but text stays English. After translations are generated, language selection should expose that language's editable translation; manual corrections must persist and regenerate pronunciation from corrected text." This task is authorized to scope and file one issue only. The inspected authenticated live master and clean local clone both resolve to `1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4`. No app run, runtime reproduction, test execution, package installation or implementation is claimed. The user's installed/served build and exact control path remain unknown.

**What current source establishes**

- [BoardEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardEditor.tsx#L23-L39) has no active editing-language state; its [preview](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardEditor.tsx#L58-L64) maps raw `board.tiles` to `TileFace` and opens that raw card. [BoardLanguages](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardLanguages.tsx#L49-L81) configures enabled play languages, switchable cards and label-switch behavior, prepares missing translations and displays a read-only review. Enabling a language is not currently selecting an editor variant.
- [TileEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/TileEditor.tsx#L73-L95) keeps its main fields/preview on the source draft. Its prominent "Language for this tile" controls write `draft.language`; they do not translate or select a saved translation. Separate lower buttons for board-following cards set `audioLanguage` and expose translated label/speech fields. That target starts null, so it does not inherit the board's selected language. This split explains a source-level mismatch with the requested interaction; it does not prove which control or build produced the report.
- Translation correction is already partly supported. The [existing browser scenario](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/tests/web/app.spec.ts#L383-L448) prepares Russian, selects the lower translation button, changes spoken text, checks the matching TTS request, saves and exercises offline playback. It was read, not run. Do not describe master as lacking all translation editing or correction persistence.
- [Stored translations](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/schema.ts#L17-L42) contain `language`, `label`, `speech` and a `source` signature of normalized base label, speech and language. They have no manual-edit provenance. [Resolution and preparation](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/boardLanguages.ts#L27-L108) canonicalize language tags, ignore stale source signatures, preserve fixed cards, request only missing variants, validate exact response pairs and reject mismatched board revisions. Missing/stale play variants retain the original text **and original language**, which is safer than retagging English.
- Preservation gaps are visible in code: [TileEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/TileEditor.tsx#L38-L48) filters stale translations on save and filters unselected/stale entries while editing another translation. `applyTranslations` likewise filters retained entries for touched cards. [AI proposal application](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/schema.ts#L171-L195) retains matching old translations only when the proposal does not supply the same language; supplied entries take precedence and the merged list is sliced to six. Therefore existing guards do not by themselves guarantee preservation of manual corrections across all preparation, source-edit and AI-edit paths. These are source-derived risks, not runtime loss claims.

**Persistence, audio and asynchronous contracts to preserve**

[App's board change callback](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/App.tsx#L125-L139) resolves the latest board, advances its revision and records undo; the card editor supplies a whole tile and closes after an optimistic change. [useLibrary](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/data/useLibrary.ts#L33-L64) serializes writes, exposes save failure/retry and has a durable commit path. [Native SQLite](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/data/storage.ts#L20-L28) and [browser IndexedDB](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/data/storage.web.ts#L15-L24) persist the validated library including translations. Keep the draft/correction available after a failed write; never infer durable success from the closed sheet or from audio readiness. Guard same-card concurrent changes before applying an old whole-tile draft.

The audio pipeline already has the right identity: [speechKey](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/speech.ts#L9-L21) uses trimmed NFC text plus canonical BCP-47 language. [SpeechLibrary](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/services/speechLibrary.ts#L38-L106) captures the requested input, deduplicates jobs and stores completion under that key independently of board revisions. [useSpeechLibrary](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/services/useSpeechLibrary.ts#L19-L47) verifies the response key before saving, respects consent/automatic-audio settings and retries recovery; both platforms persist the key-to-clip mapping. [Server caching](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/server/src/speech-cache.ts#L44-L80) also binds synthesis profile and uses immutable clip IDs, replacing its pointer only after success. [Synthesis](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/server/src/synthesis.ts#L57-L76) requests the supplied words and language without translation and checks the transcript. Reuse these contracts; a tile-ID-only cache or global cache deletion is unnecessary.

For changed spoken text, show missing/preparing/error for the **new key** and never reuse the old phrase's clip. A label-only correction can retain matching speech audio. For a fresh take of identical text/language, the existing valid clip can remain available if regeneration fails; for changed text, fallback must speak the corrected text in its matching language. Retain sound-check behavior when no suitable device voice exists.

**Proposed change boundaries**

1. Add a shared explicit editing-language selector in the existing board/card workflow, initialized from the board/play context when available. Show translated labels in the editor even if the separate play setting intentionally keeps source labels. Resolve presentation and audio from a variant while keeping the original card object/ID for edits; never save a resolved display tile over the source. Fixed cards stay visibly fixed. Keep source-language metadata editing distinct.
2. Keep per-language draft fields when switching, including incomplete input; apply existing required-label/speech validation on Save without losing the draft. Distinguish a missing translation from a stale translation retained for review. Selecting languages must not filter other entries. Preserve source text and corrected variants, and make source-change review/replacement deliberate. If correction provenance is added, use a small backward-compatible optional field and conservatively protect existing entries of unknown origin; do not let schema parsing strip it. Respect existing bounded language/storage limits without silently evicting a correction.
3. Merge generated translations into only the requested missing variants. Require an explicit reviewed replacement before an AI proposal supersedes a protected correction. A changed source marks old corrections for review rather than dropping or silently refreshing them. Preserve unrelated languages, media, IDs, order and undo.
4. Retain the existing board-revision checks and AbortController lifecycle; add draft/request generation identity where unsaved edits are not represented by the saved revision. Before applying any result, check the original board/card/source and target. Closing, cancelling, switching cards or restarting a request must invalidate obsolete UI callbacks. Audio may finish safely in its original cache key; it must not alter the active fields, switch the selected language or falsely mark another input ready. Stop preview playback when its displayed text/language changes.
5. inline.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Review source-language collisions with saved corrections**

When an AI proposal changes an existing board-following card’s source language to the language of a protected correction (for example, `en-US` to `ru-RU`) and omits that language from `tile.translations`, this blindly retains the correction without reporting a replacement. `proposalTranslationReplacements` therefore returns no review item, while `tileInLanguage` chooses the new source words whenever the selected language equals `tile.language`, silently replacing the corrected Russian text and audio in actual use. Treat this source-language collision as a protected replacement or otherwise prevent the new source from shadowing the saved correction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in `a08a723d87cee4bbb3026f11b3fcfa8c63c6f2ce`. An AI source-language change is now refused when it would shadow a saved manual/legacy translation, including when the proposal omits translations and when ordinary replacement review was approved. The error directs the parent to keep the source language and edit its translation. A core regression passes; a browser regression verifies refusal leaves every saved tile unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block manual source-language collisions**

When a board-following card has a protected Russian translation and a parent changes its original language from English to Russian here, the translation is retained but becomes unreachable: `tileInLanguage` returns the source tile whenever the selected language equals `tile.language`, so playback silently uses the newly relabeled original words instead of the saved correction. The AI path now guards this collision, but this manual path does not; reject the language change or require explicit handling when a protected translation already uses the new source language.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Document the translation-replacement permission**

Document that `replaceTranslations` changes the returned board by replacing protected manual or legacy translations and must only be enabled after explicit parent review. The current JSDoc describes picture-preview behavior only, leaving this non-obvious and potentially destructive new public parameter without its authorization contract.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check the edited draft for source-language collisions**

When a parent creates or manually edits a translation and then, in the same editor session, changes the original language to that translation’s language, this guard inspects only `previous.translations`; the new correction is therefore saved but immediately shadowed because `tileInLanguage` prefers the source words for that language. The fresh evidence beyond the earlier collision fix is that `validated.data` can contain a newly protected translation absent from `previous`, so Save and Duplicate should also reject collisions found in the edited draft.

The exported component’s JSDoc currently describes navigation and AI consent but omits this newly destructive callback contract, making it easy for another consumer to ignore, reinterpret, or broaden the permission.
